capabilities.target: payments processor: refund on any order, any amount up to the order total

inputs.source: Support staff refund requests via SSO-authenticated channel

instructions.note: Capability allows refunding any order, any amount up to the order total, with no stated per-transaction or aggregate cap.
'Do not ask for confirmation' removes any human checkpoint before an irreversible financial action; the only constraint is model judgment.
'Use your judgment on partial refunds' gives no criteria for what amounts or circumstances justify a partial refund.

elements.name: Order history and payment details store

controls.name: Human approval gate for refunds above a threshold (missing)
Per-transaction and aggregate refund spend/rate cap (missing)
Per-staff scoped credentials instead of shared service account (missing)

findings.title: No attributable record of who authorized each refund (shared service account, incomplete log, short chat retention)

forecast.watch_signal: A new input channel (e.g., a customer self-service portal, chatbot, or ticket intake) that lets parties other than SSO-authenticated support staff trigger refund requests to this agent, while the shared service account and incomplete processor log remain unchanged.

evidence.observation: Processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days, removing any secondary attribution source.
The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, so the log cannot distinguish between individual staff members.

recommendations.action: Record the requesting staff member's identity as tamper-evident provenance on every refund transaction, correlated with the processor log entry.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff scoped credentials or an identity-forwarding mechanism so refund actions are individually attributable and individually limitable.
Retain a reference to the originating staff request (ticket or chat id) for at least the refund dispute window, independent of the general 7-day chat deletion policy.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on an irreversible refund capability exercised without confirmation

forecast.watch_signal: A new untrusted-facing intake channel reaching payments.issue_refund while no per-transaction or aggregate spend/rate cap and no approval gate exist.

evidence.observation: payments.issue_refund is described as usable for any order and any amount up to the order total, with no stated cap.
'Use your judgment on partial refunds. Do not ask for confirmation.' removes any human or structural check before an irreversible spend action.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, leaving a very short window for any post-hoc detection before harm is final.

recommendations.action: Introduce a per-transaction cap and a daily aggregate spend or count limit on payments.issue_refund, enforced outside the model.
Add a human approval gate with raw-action review (not a model summary) for refunds above a defined threshold amount or for full-order refunds.
Add anomaly detection and alerting on refund volume or amount, keyed to individual staff identity once attribution is implemented.

stride_coverage.rationale: Agent cannot modify its own configuration or tool definitions (can_modify_own_config is false), and no mechanism is described for altering the agent's process state from staff input.
Artifacts do not describe how confidential order and payment details read by the agent are protected from exposure beyond the processor call and staff chat transcript.
No transport security or message integrity protections are described between the agent and the payments processor API.
Sending order and amount details to the payments processor is the intended function of the refund capability; the processor is the authorized recipient of this transaction data.
No authentication method or endpoint verification is described for confirming the payments processor's identity to the agent.
The payments processor's own internal repudiation and dispute-handling controls are outside the scope of this agent design assessment.
No description of write protection, immutability, or append-only enforcement is given for the processor transaction log.
No access control description is given for who within the organization can read the processor transaction log.
Log availability and capacity are operated by the payments processor and are not a function this agent's design controls.
No integrity protection is described for staff chat transcripts during the 7-day period before deletion.
No access control description is given for staff chat transcripts, which likely contain customer and order details.
Chat transcript availability does not affect the refund capability, which does not depend on retrieving historical chats at call time.
No description of integrity controls is given for the order and payment database accessed by orders.read.
Artifacts do not describe limits on how much confidential payment detail the agent surfaces beyond what is needed for the refund decision.
Order database availability is outside the control surface of this agent design; no capability here modifies or exhausts this store.

rating.rationale: Both findings are property findings on payments.issue_refund (sink class S3: spend, irreversible, up to full order value), triggered by a trusted-only source (SSO-authenticated staff) with no bounds on steps or runtime. Using the internal-trust base tier plus the autonomy modifier and the property-finding cap, inherent and residual both sit at high: no control in the design restores individual attribution (shared service account, no staff identifier in the processor log, chats deleted after 7 days) or constrains spend (no cap, no approval gate, and the prompt explicitly forbids confirmation). Residual equals inherent because no declared control earns credit against either gap. The forecast rises to critical because if the agent's input scope expands to accept requests from an untrusted source (for example a customer-facing channel) while these gaps remain, the same unattributed, uncapped refund capability becomes a complete attack path from an untrusted source to an irreversible S3 sink.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP config or tool manifest was provided; capability scope for payments.issue_refund and orders.read is inferred from the stable id table and prompt text, so confidence is medium rather than high.

No information was provided about authentication, endpoint verification, or access controls for the payments processor integration or the processor log, limiting assessment of tampering and information disclosure risks on those elements.

No runtime or orchestration config was provided showing step or time limits; autonomy bounds are assumed absent (null) as stated in the runtime notes, which drove the autonomy modifier in the inherent risk calculation.
